selection.selected_by: dev MRR on answerable questions; threshold by dev end-to-end correctness

headline.ci_method: bootstrap over 38 answerable test questions, 1000 resamples

gate.rule: Pass only if both hold on the test questions: (1) the lower bound of the 95% bootstrap interval on end-to-end correctness is above the correctness of the always-abstain policy (which equals the share of unanswerable questions); (2) unless the headline retriever is BM25 itself, the lower bound of the 95% paired bootstrap interval on the MRR gain over BM25 is above zero, so that any extra complexity is shown to pay for itself.

threshold_tuned_on_test.note: The threshold was chosen on the questions it is scored on. Optimistic by construction.

answer_everything.note: A system that never abstains gets every unanswerable question wrong.

answerable_only.note: Scoring only answerable questions hides the cost of answering what should be refused.

caveats: The corpus is generated from templates about a fictional company. It teaches how to evaluate retrieval and answering. It says nothing about real documents.
The test set is small (see test_questions), so every interval is wide. Differences of a few points are not evidence.
Questions are written from the same templates as the documents, so lexical retrieval is easier here than on real text.
The reader is a rule-based extractor, not a language model. LSA is a classical stand-in for dense retrieval, not a neural embedder.
No language model generates or judges answers in this project. That comparison is designed, not built.
